new:
The fifth IID scene, Sp-DFA, shows a different trade-off. With ten matched seeds and the same checkpoint across views, native/shared paired differences (minus_F−Full, mean±sample SD) are ACC +0.117±0.995 percentage points, AEOD −0.00661±0.01017 and ASPD +0.01725±0.01433. Removing F therefore improves mean accuracy and AEOD but worsens ASPD; the fixed nine- and six-seed native/shared panels retain these directions. Raw predictions instead give ACC +0.012±1.003 percentage points, AEOD +0.01077±0.01216 and ASPD +0.01053±0.00748 in the ten-seed panel: accuracy increases slightly while both disparities worsen. All three raw seed panels have these directions. The AEOD reversal between raw and calibrated prediction shows why the prediction rule matters to interpretation. We preserve it alongside the S-DFA means favoring Full; neither this comparison nor the mixed replay devices isolate a causal effect or establish significance or universal necessity.

Correlated scores, compensation by candidate selection and root-estimation variability are plausible explanations, not isolated causes.

old: At this draft's accepted cutoff, 340 deletion checkpoints have complete three-view evidence: U100, C100 and A100 each cover all ten cells, and F40 covers IID Benign, F Flip, FedSA and S-DFA with ten paired seeds per scene. The remaining 460 planned mechanism-control checkpoints comprise 60 F-deletion runs and 100 runs for each of four other controls. Native acceptance is separately 341/800, leaving 459 without native acceptance; that is not a claim that all 459 remain untrained. The one additional accepted native checkpoint does not yet count toward completed three-view coverage.
